I happened to need Bessel function and some of its properties in my project. After toying around a bit, I wonder if I can get them in Mathlib. Does this sound like some reasonable contribution?

Let me start with just the definition of the Bessel function of the first kind. Before I copy the definition from wikipedia (a ℂ -> ℂ function defined by the power series, with the parameter α also possibly a complex number), is there anything I should be aware of such as alternative convention or formalization pitfall?

I haven't really thought about it, but I suspect it is not completely trivial to decide what to take as the definition. You don't want a definition that only holds for integer parameters (or in a restricted domain). I would suspect that first doing a lot of theory for the generalized hypergeometric function and then defining Bessel functions in terms of the (1,0)-hypergeometric function is the way to go, but again I haven't thought deeply about it.
There is a formalization in https://github.com/mrdouglasny/OSforGFF/blob/main/OSforGFF/General/BesselFunction.lean but it is far from mathlib level generality

This definition

with complex x and α, seems to give a function well-defineddifferentiable on docs#Complex.slitPlane (and for the entire plane for integer α)
Generalized hypergeometric function seems to be a bit beyond what I can do... is it fine to go with the definition above for now, and connect to generalized hypergeometric function later?

If you just need the Bessel functions for your own project than you can do whatever you like. If you want to get the Bessel functions into mathlib, then you might have to argue why your approach is the right one. Obviously if your project shows that your definition of Bessel functions covers the full range of parameters, then that is good indication that your definition is good for mathlib.
Honestly, I would not bother with getting it into mathlib at this stage, unless you want to spend some time thinking about the best definition.

Yep, I understand that. This is more like "I am bored and I'd like to see how far I can go if I try spending time thinking about the best definition", and "not contributing anything" is a totally acceptable outcome
I opened this thread mainly because I want to learn what people think the appropriate definition should be
You know what, maybe you are right about doing hypergeometric function first, because I quickly run into summability argument that should be stated in the general form for hypergeometric function
